curriculum.lesson_evidence: Make predictions from evidence and ask questions that deepen understanding.
curriculum.scope_limit: Individual Written Core lesson contributes partial evidence; independently verify syllabus content-point alignment.

lesson.child_mission: Make predictions from evidence and ask questions that deepen understanding.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Keep the independent response and two written check responses; record oral retelling or performance where required by the task.
lesson.extension: Create a new example using a completely different character or setting, show the same skill, then explain to another person how you checked its accuracy.
lesson.guided_practice:
WE DO — attempt each prompt before comparing to the feedback.
1. Predict what happens after "The dog scratched at the back door and whined".
COMPARE: Perhaps it wants to go outside. Scratching at the door and whining are clues; this is not certain.
2. Ask one question after "Leah stared at the empty nest".
COMPARE: "Where did the birds go?" or "How does Leah feel?" are useful questions because the text raises uncertainty.
3. Your prediction is a lost dog. New line: "Its owner whistled and it came running." Update your idea.
COMPARE: The dog may not be lost; it recognises its owner and responds to the whistle.
4. Identify fact and prediction: "The path was wet, so I think someone used the hose."
COMPARE: Fact: path was wet. Prediction/inference: someone used the hose; rain or another cause is also possible.
lesson.independent_task:
YOU DO — complete the following substantial original task, not a copied model.
Read: "The library lights flickered. Ella heard a click from the corridor. She shut her book and walked towards the desk." Write two predictions with different clues, three useful questions and an updated prediction after adding your own plausible next sentence. Label facts versus possible explanations.
lesson.learning_intention: Make predictions from evidence and ask questions that deepen understanding.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper to copy only the original independent prompt; have the child respond in writing or orally as required. Save a photograph or brief parent observation for the learning record.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance: Reward evidence-linked predictions and willingness to revise. Many imaginative answers are acceptable but details claimed as facts must appear in the passage. Accept plausible original solutions where the text supports them; require the learner to explain at least one independent choice.

Parent: Written model 1: Original demonstration: Text: "Clouds darkened and Mara packed her picnic blanket." Prediction: Mara expects rain. Evidence: dark clouds and packing. I may be wrong, but I have a reason.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Do not cling to your first prediction after contrary evidence appears. Correction: The dog may not be lost; it recognises its owner and responds to the whistle.

Parent: Assess comprehension and language rather than penalising speech or motor difficulties unrelated to the objective. Keep written models out of the child role.
